items.title: Accusing wife of adultery for speaking to male friend is cruelty: Jharkhand High Court
items.summary: The Jharkhand High Court recently observed that accusing one's wife of adultery for merely speaking to her male friend amounts to mental cruelty. A Bench of Chief Justice MS Sonak and Justice Manoj Prasad made the observation while dismissing a man’s plea seeking divorce from his wife. One of the allegations made by the husband was that his wife was in an extra-marital relationship as she used to talk to an unknown male over mobile phone. “To our considered view, such allegations are typical gender-based stereotypes, where, if a woman talks to a man, even if he is a friend, charges of adultery or of an extramarital relationship are levelled. We are, therefore, of the considered view that such allegations amount to cruelty towards the wife,” the Court said. Chief Justice MS Sonak, Justice Manoj Prasad The couple had married in 2005 and have two children. In 2021, the husband moved a family court seeking dissolution of marriage, alleging that his wife was not interested in the marital relationship. items.title: Aadhaar card not conclusive proof of age; postmortem report more reliable: Madhya Pradesh High Court
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court recently held that an Aadhaar card cannot be treated as conclusive proof of a person's age, observing that that a postmortem report is a more reliable indicator [ Rajesh Singh & Anr. v Rahul Singh & Ors. ]. Justice Amit Seth made the observation while enhancing the compensation awarded to the parents of a 13-year-old boy who died in a motor accident in December 2019. A Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal had earlier relied on the boy's Aadhaar card to determine his age to be 14 years old. The insurance company, on the other hand, pointed to the postmortem report which recorded him as 13 years old. The Court found merit in the insurance company's argument and observed that an Aadhaar card cannot, by itself, establish the age of its holder conclusively. "An Aadhaar Card is primarily an identity document and cannot, by itself, be treated as conclusive proof of the age of its holder. On the other hand, the age recorded in the postmortem report is based upon medical assessment conducted in the course of postmortem examination," said the Court. items.title: Can't let women, children fall prey to buses and die: Kerala High Court calls for strict measures
items.summary: The Kerala High Court Tuesday expressed serious concern over reckless driving by bus drivers and speeding cars and the rising number of road accidents in the State, calling for concrete measures to prevent further loss of lives [ Suo Motu v The Chief Secretary and ors and connected cases ]. A bench of Justice Raja Vijayaraghavan V and Justice KV Jayakumar suggested permanent cancellation of driving license or impounding offending vehicles to curb road mishaps. "If it is done repeatedly, your licence will go, or vehicle. Some action will have to be taken. Everything is being taken lightly and the corrective measures are not being taken," the Court remarked. The Court was hearing a suo motu petition concerning road safety in Kerala. "We can't just permit all the children, women to fall prey to the buses and go underneath the tyres and die. Why would we want to do that? Come up with something," the Court said. Justice Vijayaraghavan questioned the authorities over their failure to effectively implement existing road safety guidelines.
